signals.entity: Magyar Nemzeti Bank (MNB) - all Hungarian payment service providers
signals.signal: MNB Decree 19/2025 (VI.26.) sets the criteria for COMPULSORY ATM installation and the cost-sharing between payment service providers, operationalising Hungary's cash-access mandate. It allocates 80 settlement packages (from the list in NGM Decree 16/2025 (V.29.)) to named PSPs using a weighted formula: cash-service revenue 20%, debit cards issued 30%, consumer accounts 10%, deposits 15%, balance-sheet total 25%. The decree text carries a second-phase contracting deadline of 28/02/2026 for providers swapping/sharing assigned settlements and notification to the MNB by 16/03/2026; a successor operator must reimburse a predecessor's documented installation costs incurred within 3 years. Hungarian press consistently reports the underlying installation deadlines as settlements above 1,000 inhabitants by 31/12/2025 and settlements above 500 inhabitants by 31/12/2026 (2022 census population) - PRESS-SOURCED, not verified in the decree text I extracted.
signals.source_name: Nemzeti Jogszabalytar (net.jogtar.hu) - 19/2025. (VI. 26.) MNB rendelet ['MNB Decree on the criteria for the installation of automated banknote dispensing machines and the detailed rules on the burden- and cost-sharing of payment service providers']
signals.implies: (a) Every Hungarian retail bank/PSP issuing consumer payment accounts and cards - OTP, MBH, K&H, Erste Hungary, Raiffeisen Hungary, UniCredit Hungary, Granit, plus Magyar Posta as a channel. (b) They must physically deploy and operate NEW ATMs in low-footfall rural settlements where the standalone business case is negative. That forces: cheap-to-run dispensers, shared/white-label estates across banks, remote telemetry instead of engineer call-outs, and cash forecasting to cut CIT (cash-in-transit) runs. Printec map: NCR Atleos dispensers for low-volume sites, x-core multivendor ATM software to run a shared/mixed estate under one bank's brand, ATM device telemetry & monitoring, NCR APTRA OptiCash cash optimisation, physical ATM security for unattended rural locations, and the 500+ engineer managed/field-service organisation. (c) For the 31/12/2026 tranche, budget had to commit around Q1-Q2 2026 - this is now an EXECUTION-phase opportunity (hardware, install, monitoring, multi-year service contracts), not a planning-phase one. Second-phase swap contracts were due 28/02/2026, so the per-bank site lists are already fixed.
signals.likelihood: Certain - decree in force, per-settlement allocations already published
signals.followup: Pull the annex of NGM Decree 16/2025 (V.29.) plus the MNB per-settlement allocation table to size the remaining >500-inhabitant tranche by bank (site count). CONFIRM the 31/12/2025 and 31/12/2026 installation dates against the underlying statute/decree annex before quoting them to a customer - the decree body I extracted shows the CONTRACTING dates (28/02/2026, 16/03/2026), not the installation dates. Candidate for promotion to its own 'cash access mandates' workstream.

signals.entity: Republic of Slovenia - Ministry of Finance (Ministrstvo za finance) with Banka Slovenije
signals.signal: Draft Act on the Accessibility of Cash and Free Basic Payment Services (SL: 'Predlog zakona o dostopnosti gotovine in brezplacnih osnovnih placilnih storitvah') is in PUBLIC CONSULTATION until 17/08/2026. It would oblige banks and Posta Slovenije to guarantee a cash access point 'dostopne v razdalji najvec pet kilometrov od centra naselja' (accessible within a maximum of five kilometres from the centre of the settlement) for settlements above 1,000 inhabitants, with equivalent coverage criteria for branches in larger settlements and an obligation of continuous operation of that infrastructure. It also creates a free basic payment package (account, debit card, online/mobile banking, unlimited incoming transfers, own-bank cash transactions, and a minimum of FIVE FREE MONTHLY ATM WITHDRAWALS AT OTHER BANKS' ATMs) for people receiving regular income, with an extended package for vulnerable groups and pensioners. This is the implementing law for the new constitutional Article 74.a.
signals.source_name: OZS - Obrtno-podjetniska zbornica Slovenije, citing the Ministry of Finance draft published for consultation on e-uprava.gov.si ['Accessibility of cash and free basic payment services - draft law in public consultation']
signals.implies: (a) All Slovenian banks - NLB, NKBM (OTP), SKB (OTP), Intesa Sanpaolo Bank, Addiko Bank, Gorenjska banka, Delavska hranilnica - plus Posta Slovenije. (b) A 5 km geographic coverage rule reverses ATM/branch rationalisation and forces new low-volume cash points, while five free out-of-network withdrawals per customer per month destroys the interchange economics of those points. The only way to make that work is lower cost-per-cash-point: cash RECYCLERS (cash-in funds cash-out, halving CIT trips), multivendor software so a single estate serves several brands, and remote monitoring. Printec map: Glory / Sesami TCRs and NCR recycling ATMs, NCR Atleos hardware, x-core multivendor ATM software, ATM telemetry & monitoring, APTRA OptiCash, self-service kiosks combining cash and non-cash services, managed/field services. (c) Consultation closes 17/08/2026; if adopted around end-2026 with a typical 12-month transition, budget must commit H1-2027. Banks that want to shape the coverage map must engage NOW.
signals.likelihood: High that a cash-access law passes in some form (it implements a constitutional article); the 5 km radius and five-free-withdrawals parameters may change in the parliamentary reading
signals.followup: Open the primary draft on e-uprava.gov.si / gov.si (Ministrstvo za finance, eDemokracija) and extract exact article numbers, transition period, penalties, and whether Posta Slovenije outlets and third-party (IAD) ATMs count toward the 5 km rule - that single definition sets the addressable device count. Also check Banka Slovenije's formal opinion on the draft.

signals.entity: National Bank of Ukraine (NBU) - all Ukrainian banks, PSPs and self-service terminal operators
signals.signal: NBU Board Resolution No. 67 of 16/06/2026 ('On approving Amendments to certain regulatory acts of the National Bank of Ukraine on cash circulation'), officially published 18/06/2026 and IN FORCE FROM 26/06/2026, amends the Instruction on cash-work organisation (Resolution No. 103 of 25/09/2018) and the Rules on determining payment features and exchange of banknotes (Resolution No. 134 of 03/12/2018). New points 124-1 to 124-4 require that for ANY cash-in transaction initiated at a PTKS (self-service payment terminal), REGARDLESS OF AMOUNT, the payer must key their full mobile number on the terminal screen in +380 format and the PSP/commercial agent must verify ownership of that number by sending a one-time password by SMS or reading it out by automated phone call, with the payer entering it on the terminal screen; the FULL mobile number must be printed on the receipt as a mandatory field; and PSPs must continuously take measures to prevent the OTP being passed to another person, including shortening its validity. The same resolution introduces a NEW Ukrainian licence category, 'bank of financial inclusion' (UA: 'банк фінансової інклюзії'), operating under a limited banking licence, and brings it into the cash-work Instruction.
signals.source_name: National Bank of Ukraine - Postanova Pravlinnya NBU No. 67 vid 16 chervnya 2026 roku (PDF on bank.gov.ua) ['On approving Amendments to certain NBU regulatory acts on cash circulation']
signals.implies: (a) Every Ukrainian bank and non-bank PSP running self-service cash-in terminals and cash-accepting ATMs - PrivatBank, Oschadbank, Raiffeisen Bank Ukraine, Universal Bank/monobank, PUMB, plus the large independent terminal networks (EasyPay, City24, iBox). Ukrainian sources count roughly 22,930 self-service payment terminals and 15,750 ATMs. (b) Every cash-in terminal application needs a NEW screen flow (phone entry, OTP entry, retry/expiry handling), a new receipt template with the full mobile number, an OTP/voice-call delivery integration, and anti-mule controls on OTP sharing. That is squarely a multivendor self-service SOFTWARE and kiosk-application change, not a hardware change. Printec map: x-core multivendor ATM/kiosk software and screen-flow customisation, self-service & bank kiosks, ATM/device telemetry to prove the new flow is live across the estate, and AML/transaction-monitoring (IMTF Siron, FICO, INETCO) to detect the OTP-sharing / cash-mule patterns the NBU is explicitly targeting. The 'bank of financial inclusion' licence is a NEW category of small institution that will need a turnkey, low-cost channel stack. (c) Already in force since 26/06/2026 - this is remediation spend NOW, and any operator still non-compliant is an immediate opportunity.
signals.followup: Map which Ukrainian terminal networks have actually shipped the OTP flow (spot-check operator app-release notes) to find the laggards. Separately, pull the NBU's licensing regulation for the 'bank of financial inclusion' to size that new segment. Note this touches personal-data processing (mobile number capture, printing the full number on receipts) - refer any customer question on GDPR/Ukrainian data-protection exposure to Printec's DPO / Compliance team rather than advising.

signals.entity: National Bank of Ukraine (NBU) - banks, CIT companies and device service organisations
signals.signal: The NBU will introduce a NEW UAH 2,000 banknote into circulation on 04/09/2026, and presented it roughly two months in advance specifically so institutions can reconfigure equipment. Per NBU statements reported by Ukrainian financial media, 38,690 self-service devices must be reconfigured to recognise, accept and dispense the note - 15,750 ATMs and 22,930 self-service payment terminals (PTKS) - plus back-office sorting machines. The NBU says it will provide banks, CIT companies and service organisations with the technical capability to perform the configuration FREE OF CHARGE, and all work must be finished by 04/09/2026.
signals.source_name: Interfax-Ukraine ['Banks will have the opportunity to prepare ATMs and PTKS for the introduction of the UAH 2,000 banknote - NBU'], corroborated by Minfin.com.ua
signals.implies: (a) Every Ukrainian ATM deployer, independent terminal operator, CIT firm and cash-centre operator. (b) A new denomination means firmware/BV (bill validator) template updates on every acceptor and dispenser, cassette re-planning and denomination-mix changes in cash forecasting, plus a fleet-wide rollout and verification exercise inside a ~2-month window. Printec map: field/managed services for the fleet-wide firmware rollout (this is exactly what a 500+ engineer organisation is for), ATM device telemetry & monitoring to verify note-set updates device-by-device and catch failures, NCR APTRA OptiCash to re-optimise denomination mix and replenishment once a 2,000-note exists, and Glory/NCR recycler and sorter note-set updates. (c) Immediate - the window is now to 04/09/2026; any bank without a verified fleet-wide rollout plan is a live services opportunity this quarter.
signals.likelihood: Certain - date announced by the NBU
signals.followup: Retrieve the NBU's own press release on bank.gov.ua (the site 403s the fetch tool; use a desktop User-Agent via curl as was done successfully for the Resolution No. 67 PDF) to confirm the 04/09/2026 date and the 15,750 / 22,930 device counts from the primary source rather than press. Then check which note-set/firmware versions NCR Atleos, Glory and the BV vendors have released for UAH 2,000.

signals.entity: Parliament of Romania (Senate) - all ATM-operating payment service providers in Romania
signals.signal: Legislative proposal B409/2026, registered at the Senate (first chamber seised) on 24/06/2026 and signed by MPs from PSD, AUR, UDMR, USR, PNL, SOS, POT, minorities and non-affiliated members, would amend Law no. 209/2019 on payment services to OBLIGE every PSP operating cash-withdrawal ATMs in Romania to let the user key in a PERSONALISED withdrawal amount, for cards issued by ANY authorised provider - ending the widespread practice of offering out-of-network cardholders only fixed pre-set amounts. Breach affecting (or capable of affecting) consumer interests is punishable by a fine of RON 50,000 to RON 100,000. Status: at the Senate; it still needs adoption by both chambers, promulgation and publication in Monitorul Oficial.
signals.source_name: Profit.ro ['Major change at ATMs awaited for years. All banks obliged to dispense personalised amounts at ATMs also for other banks' customers - draft'], corroborated by Business24.ro and Cotidianul
signals.implies: (a) Every ATM deployer in Romania - BCR, BRD, Banca Transilvania, ING Romania, Raiffeisen Romania, UniCredit Romania, CEC Bank, OTP Romania, plus independent deployers (Euronet). (b) The explanatory memorandum itself says the limitation is NOT technical but a matter of how the ATM interface is configured for external users - which makes this a pure ATM APPLICATION / screen-flow change across the whole national estate, executed once, consistently, across mixed hardware. That is precisely the multivendor-software value proposition. Printec map: x-core multivendor ATM software (single screen-flow change deployed across NCR/Diebold/Wincor estates), ATM telemetry & monitoring to evidence compliance device-by-device to ANPC, and NCR APTRA OptiCash - free-amount entry changes the denomination mix and replenishment maths, so cash forecasting must be retuned. (c) If it clears both chambers in the 2026-2027 session with a typical short transition, budget should be pencilled in for 2027; the pre-emptive sale is available NOW because the change is cheap and reputationally attractive.
signals.likelihood: Medium-high that it is adopted - it is cross-party and cheap to implement; timing in the Romanian legislative calendar is the uncertainty
signals.followup: PRIMARY SOURCE STILL OPEN: pull B409/2026 from senat.ro (Fisa initiativei legislative) and cdep.ro to confirm the registration date, the exact wording of the amendment to Legea 209/2019, the enforcement authority (likely ANPC) and any transition period. Do not quote the RON 50,000-100,000 fine range to a customer until it is read off the Senate text.

signals.entity: European Union - providers and deployers of high-risk AI, including all footprint banks
signals.country: EU-wide (AT, BG, HR, CY, CZ, GR, HU, RO, SK, SI in footprint; mirrored over time by RS, BA, MK, AL, XK, ME, UA through accession alignment)
signals.signal: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (the 'Digital Omnibus on AI'), adopted 08/07/2026, published in the Official Journal on 24/07/2026 and in force from 27/07/2026, amends the AI Act (Reg (EU) 2024/1689) and POSTPONES the high-risk regime. Chapter III Sections 1-3 now apply from 02/12/2027 for AI systems classified as high-risk under Article 6(2) and Annex III - which includes AI used to evaluate natural persons' creditworthiness or establish a credit score (fraud detection is carved out) - and from 02/08/2028 for Article 6(1)/Annex I product-embedded high-risk AI, replacing the original 02/08/2026 date. Prohibitions, AI-literacy, GPAI and transparency obligations already in application are unaffected; the Omnibus also expands the AI Office's enforcement role and adjusts the GDPR legal basis for bias-detection processing.
signals.implies: (a) Every footprint bank running AI/ML in credit decisioning, and separately every bank buying software with AI inside it. (b) The 16-month delay removes the near-term control build-out but NOT the inventory, classification, logging, human-oversight and technical-documentation groundwork - and it shifts evidentiary burden onto VENDORS. For Printec this is primarily a QUALIFICATION requirement, not a sale: the AI/ML components inside AML/KYC and transaction monitoring (IMTF Siron, FICO, INETCO) and digital onboarding/eKYC (Namirial, biometric face-match) must be able to produce conformity and data-governance evidence on demand, and remote-identification biometrics sit in a sensitive Annex III area. Adjacent Printec pull-through: document management and audit-trail tooling for model evidence. (c) Bank spend on AI-governance tooling slides to 2027; the immediate 2026 activity is inventory and vendor questionnaires - which means Printec will be ASKED for evidence in 2026 even though the deadline is 2027.
signals.followup: PROMOTE to its own workstream next run ('AI Act + supervisory AI expectations'), bundling this with the ESAs frontier-AI statement and the ECB SSM-2026-0301 letter already captured. Track designation of national market-surveillance authorities in AT/GR/RO/HU/BG/CZ/SI/SK/HR/CY - several were late and that determines who enforces. For any bank asking whether their specific scoring model falls inside the Annex III carve-out, do NOT rule - state the Article 6(2)/Annex III text and refer to Printec Compliance/Legal.

signals.entity: EU co-legislators - Regulation on the legal tender of euro banknotes and coins, procedure 2023/0208(COD)
signals.country: Euro area in footprint: AT, BG, HR, CY, GR, SK, SI (and prospectively RO, CZ, HU on adoption)
signals.signal: The legal-tender-of-cash Regulation is the THIRD file of the Single Currency Package and is legally distinct from the digital-euro files. ECON adopted its report in November 2025 (reported 46-4-8, rapporteur Navarrete, after a revised draft report presented 05/11/2025); the Council agreed its negotiating position in December 2025, including that Member States must MONITOR AND SAFEGUARD ACCESS TO AND ACCEPTANCE OF cash and put resilience measures in place for payment continuity, and wanting an effective ban on non-acceptance of cash by retailers with limited exceptions (distance/online sales and unmanned points of sale). Trilogues on the package opened 13/07/2026 under the Irish Presidency with the stated aim of political agreement before end-2026. The EP Legislative Train page was last updated 20/06/2026 and shows no agreement date announced.
signals.source_name: European Parliament Legislative Train Schedule - 'Scope and effects of legal tender of euro banknotes and coins' (file 2023/0208(COD))
signals.implies: (a) Every euro-area footprint bank (AT, BG, HR, CY, GR, SK, SI) and, on adoption of the euro, RO/CZ/HU. Also every merchant-acquiring customer. (b) A binding EU-level access-to-cash monitoring duty converts today's voluntary/national arrangements (Hungary's decree, Slovenia's draft law, Greece's ATM fee law) into a footprint-wide obligation: banks will have to EVIDENCE geographic cash coverage to their NCB and keep loss-making cash points alive. That is a structural, multi-year driver for cash recyclers, low-cost dispensers, shared estates and cash-cycle optimisation. Printec map: NCR Atleos ATMs (recycling/intelligent deposit), Glory/Sesami TCRs, x-core multivendor software, ATM telemetry & monitoring (the natural evidence-generation layer for a coverage-reporting duty), APTRA OptiCash, and managed/field services. Also a cash-ACCEPTANCE mandate on merchants keeps cash in the retail loop, which protects POS-plus-cash hybrid propositions. (c) If political agreement lands end-2026 and the regulation applies after a transition, budget commitment falls in 2027-2028. Pipeline-shaping now.
signals.likelihood: High that a political agreement is reached in the end-2026 window given the Irish Presidency's stated target and both co-legislators having positions; the coverage metrics are the open question
signals.followup: PROMOTE to its own workstream ('access to and legal tender of cash') - it is the single biggest ATM-relevant EU file not currently on the watchlist, and the national mandates (HU, SI, SK, GR, RO) belong under it. Next run: get the Council general approach text (ST document number) and the ECON report A9/A10 number, and extract any concrete coverage metric (distance, population threshold, reporting frequency). Retry the Consilium press release of 19/12/2025 with a desktop User-Agent (it 403'd this run).

signals.entity: EU co-legislators - Financial Data Access Regulation (FiDA), procedure 2023/0205(COD)
signals.country: EU-wide footprint (AT, BG, HR, CY, CZ, GR, HU, RO, SK, SI); non-EU footprint via later accession alignment
signals.signal: FiDA - the regulation that extends open-banking-style data access beyond payment accounts into savings, investments, pensions, insurance, mortgages and loans ('open finance') - is STILL IN TRILOGUE as of mid-2026. A Council working document dated 06/04/2026 (WK 5041/2026 INIT) circulates the Commission's non-paper on options for finalising the trilogue negotiations. The first trilogue was in April 2025. Scope, timing and role definitions are all still open; obligations are expected to phase in from 2027 onward as Financial Data Sharing Schemes are set up. NO adoption date and NO application date can be stated from a primary source at this point.
signals.source_name: Council of the EU - Interinstitutional file 2023/0205 (COD), working document WK 5041/2026 INIT
signals.implies: (a) Every footprint bank, plus insurers and pension providers - FiDA reaches far wider than PSD2 did. (b) It forces standardised, permissioned data-sharing APIs across product lines that have no API today, plus a customer PERMISSION DASHBOARD, plus scheme membership and compensation arrangements. Printec map is indirect but real: digital onboarding/eKYC (Namirial) as the identity layer for data-sharing consent, document management for the consent/audit record, and the AML/transaction-monitoring stack (IMTF Siron, FICO, INETCO) because broader data access widens the fraud and data-exfiltration surface. Printec is NOT an open-banking API platform vendor, so the honest read is partner/pull-through, not a lead product. (c) No date to anchor a budget - watch for provisional political agreement; only then does the ~24-month clock start.
signals.likelihood: Uncertain - the file was politically near-dead in 2025 and revived; scope may be cut substantially
signals.followup: Candidate for a WATCH slot rather than a full workstream until a provisional agreement exists. Next run: check the EP Legislative Train page for 2023/0205(COD) and the ECON committee calendar for a trilogue outcome, and open WK 5041/2026 INIT itself to see which options the Commission put on the table.

signals.entity: European Banking Authority (EBA) - deposit guarantee schemes and all deposit-taking banks
signals.country: EU-wide footprint (AT, BG, HR, CY, CZ, GR, HU, RO, SK, SI)
signals.signal: On 23/07/2026 the EBA launched its FIRST FOUR consultations under the revised Deposit Guarantee Schemes Directive (DGSD3), out of 12 mandated technical standards and guidelines: (1) ITS on depositor information - harmonised content and format of the depositor information sheet at account opening and periodically, plus required communications in mergers and failures; (2) ITS on information exchange - standardised procedures, templates and minimum requirements for information exchange in bank-failure scenarios; (3) RTS on client funds held in intermediary accounts - rules so DGSs can identify and reimburse underlying clients and clarity on whether payout goes direct or via the account holder; (4) Guidelines on investment of DGS available financial means. The comment deadline on all four is 23/10/2026.
signals.source_name: European Banking Authority - press release, 'The EBA consults on rules to further improve depositor protection under the revised Deposit Guarantee Schemes Directive' (listed on the EBA press-release index)
signals.implies: (a) Every deposit-taking bank in the EU footprint and each national DGS (Greek TEKE, Bulgarian BDIF, Croatian HAOD, Romanian FGDB, Hungarian OBA, Czech Garancni system, Slovak FOD, Slovenian and Cypriot schemes, Austrian ESA). (b) DGSD3 is a DATA and DOCUMENT-PRODUCTION regime: banks must produce Single Customer View files to a new standard, identify beneficial clients behind intermediary/client-money accounts, and issue standardised depositor information sheets at onboarding and periodically. That maps to Printec's DOCUMENT MANAGEMENT line (templated, versioned, auditable customer disclosures generated at account opening and on events), to digital onboarding/eKYC (Namirial) where the sheet must be delivered and acknowledged at account opening, and to data-quality/remediation services on the customer master. (c) Consultations close 23/10/2026; final standards likely 2027 with application aligned to national DGSD3 transposition. Budget commitment realistically 2027-2028. This is early-warning, not a live deal.
signals.likelihood: High that all four standards are finalised broadly as consulted
signals.followup: Next run: open the four consultation papers on eba.europa.eu and extract the depositor-information-sheet format requirements and the Single Customer View data fields - those are the two items that generate concrete IT work. Also confirm each footprint state's DGSD3 transposition deadline. DGSD3 is a reasonable candidate for a WATCH slot.

signals.entity: EBA, EIOPA and ESMA (the ESAs) jointly, and the ESRB - all EU financial entities under DORA
signals.country: EU-wide footprint (AT, BG, HR, CY, CZ, GR, HU, RO, SK, SI)
signals.signal: On 31/07/2026 the three ESAs issued a joint call for 'enhanced governance and consistent supervision to mitigate ICT risks from frontier AI models in the EU financial sector', expecting financial entities to have robust governance and risk-management frameworks covering prevention, detection and management of AI-enabled cyber threats, and stating that ongoing and planned DORA oversight activities for CRITICAL ICT THIRD-PARTY PROVIDERS (CTPPs) will be updated to address this risk. Earlier, on 07/07/2026, the ESAs supported an ESRB warning on systemic cyber risks from frontier AI models. The 31/07/2026 press release sets supervisory EXPECTATIONS and a supervisory-dialogue approach - it states no deadline and no prescriptive requirement.
signals.source_name: European Banking Authority - press release, 'EBA, EIOPA and ESMA call for enhanced governance and consistent supervision to mitigate ICT risks from frontier AI models in the EU financial sector'
signals.implies: (a) All footprint banks under DORA, and critically ALSO their ICT vendors - Printec itself, wherever it is an ICT third-party service provider to a financial entity. (b) It converges with the ECB SSM-2026-0301 letter (Buch to SI CEOs, 07/07/2026, action plan to the JST by 31/10/2026, explicitly naming replacement of legacy/unsupported/end-of-life technology) into one message: supervisors now treat AI-enabled attack capability as a reason to accelerate legacy REPLACEMENT and to harden third-party assurance. For Printec that is (i) a demand driver - end-of-life ATM fleets, unsupported OS on self-service devices and legacy card/HSM estates become supervisory findings, pulling forward NCR Atleos refresh, Thales HSM/PCI and remote key injection, and x-core migrations off unsupported platforms; and (ii) an obligation - Printec must be able to answer bank third-party questionnaires on its own AI and cyber governance. (c) No hard deadline here; the binding date in the same theme is the ECB JST action plan of 31/10/2026, so bank budget conversations are live in Q3-Q4 2026.
signals.likelihood: High that this converts into concrete DORA oversight questions to CTPPs and into SREP/JST dialogue during 2026-2027
signals.followup: Open the underlying joint ESAs STATEMENT document (the press release references it but does not reproduce it) and the ESRB warning of ~07/07/2026 to see whether either names concrete expectations or dates. Fold into the promoted AI workstream. Also: Printec should have its own answer ready for the third-party AI-governance questionnaire wave - flag to Printec Compliance.

signals.entity: Finanzmarktaufsicht (FMA) Austria - banks, insurers and crypto-asset service providers
signals.signal: From 01/01/2026 the FMA is the NEW supervisory authority for monitoring and enforcing FINANCIAL SANCTIONS in the Austrian financial sector, taking the function over from the Oesterreichische Nationalbank (OeNB). This completes a reform decided in 2024 and consolidates AML/CFT supervision and financial-sanctions supervision in a single authority, with the FMA describing harmonised processes and coordinated audit cycles for supervised entities. Announced by the FMA on 30/12/2025.
signals.source_name: FMA Osterreich - 'From 1 January 2026, the FMA is the new supervisory authority for monitoring and imposing financial sanctions' (English version; German original 'FMA ist ab 1. Janner 2026 die neue Aufsichtsbehorde zur Uberwachung und Durchsetzung von Finanzsanktionen'), also carried by OTS
signals.implies: (a) All Austrian banks (Erste Group, Raiffeisen Bank International and the Raiffeisen sector, UniCredit Bank Austria, BAWAG, Volksbanken, Oberbank), insurers and CASPs - and, through group supervision, RBI's and Erste's CEE subsidiaries across the footprint. (b) A single authority running combined AML + sanctions audit cycles raises the evidentiary bar on SANCTIONS SCREENING specifically: real-time and batch screening of customers, counterparties and payment messages, list-management currency, alert audit trails, and testing/tuning documentation. Printec map: IMTF Siron (sanctions/embargo and AML screening - already a footprint reference at Alpha Bank), FICO, and INETCO transaction monitoring; plus document management for the audit evidence pack. (c) First combined FMA audit cycles land during 2026-2027, so remediation budget is being set now. This is also a NEW REGULATOR and a new source environment worth adding to the standing source list (fma.gv.at news + Rundschreiben page), replacing OeNB for this topic.
signals.followup: The FMA English page 403'd the fetch tool this run (content taken from the search index); retry with a desktop User-Agent and confirm the Austrian legal basis (the amending act name) and whether any new reporting obligation or FMA Rundschreiben has followed. Add fma.gv.at Rundschreiben to the standing Agent-3 source list for Austria.

signals.entity: National Bank of the Republic of North Macedonia (NBRNM) and the Central Register of RNM - all Macedonian banks and PSPs
signals.signal: Under the Law on Payment Services and Systems (in force with the SEPA step of October 2025), a SINGLE REGISTER OF ACCOUNTS must be established and hosted by the Central Register of the Republic of North Macedonia NO LATER THAN 01/12/2026. Separately, the National Bank identified six systemically important banks on 30/10/2025, each required to hold a systemic capital buffer with FULL IMPLEMENTATION by 30/09/2026. The same law introduced the PSD2-style payment-initiation and account-information service categories, licensed by the NBRNM Executive Board.
signals.source_name: Global Legal Insights - Banking Laws and Regulations 2026: North Macedonia (law-firm country chapter; AGGREGATOR/press tier - the underlying primary is the Zakon za platezhni uslugi i platni sistemi and NBRNM decisions)
signals.implies: (a) All Macedonian banks (Komercijalna banka, Stopanska banka Skopje, NLB Banka Skopje, Halkbank, ProCredit, Sparkasse, UNIBanka) and licensed PIs/EMIs. (b) A single account register means every bank must feed standardised account and account-holder data to a central registry on a defined interface and keep it current - a data-extraction, mapping, quality and reconciliation project, and one that AML/law-enforcement enquiry workflows plug into. Printec map: AML/KYC (IMTF Siron) and digital onboarding/eKYC (Namirial) for the identity data quality behind the register, document management for the enquiry/response audit trail, and integration/managed services for the feed itself. The PISP/AISP licensing categories separately open an open-banking-adjacent integration market. (c) 01/12/2026 is 4 months out - banks that have not started are in remediation mode NOW; the systemic-buffer date of 30/09/2026 is a capital, not an IT, deadline but signals NBRNM's CRR3/CRD6 alignment pace, which drives reporting-system work into 2027.
signals.likelihood: High for the register (statutory date); the practical go-live may slip as such registries often do
signals.followup: AGGREGATOR-ONLY - must be upgraded. Next run: open the Zakon za platezhni uslugi i platni sistemi on the NBRNM site (nbrm.mk, which 403s the fetch tool - use a desktop User-Agent) and the Central Register (crm.com.mk) for the register's technical specification and onboarding timetable, and the NBRNM decision of 30/10/2025 on systemically important banks.

signals.entity: PCI Security Standards Council - acquirers, ATM deployers, POS estates and HSM/key-management operations
signals.country: All 17 footprint countries (scheme rules, not law)
signals.signal: [STANDING - dated 2025/2026] PCI DSS v4.0.1 is the only version in force: v3.2.1 was retired 31/03/2024 and the 51 future-dated v4.x requirements became effective 31/03/2025, so EVERY requirement is in scope for assessments performed during 2026 - there is no separate new 2026 core deadline. The PCI SSC ran a request-for-comments period on v4.0.1 that closed on 20/07/2026, which is the normal precursor to the next revision of the standard. On the PIN side, the current standard remains PCI PIN Security Requirements v3.1 (there is no v4), and the TR-31 Phase 3 key-block deadline passed on 31/12/2024. Anything claiming a fresh 2026 PCI PIN or PCI DSS cliff should be treated as incorrect until shown in a PCI SSC document.
signals.source_name: PCI Security Standards Council blog, 'Now is the Time for Organizations to Adopt the Future-Dated Requirements of PCI DSS v4.x' and the PCI SSC PIN Security Standard page
signals.implies: (a) Every footprint acquirer, ATM deployer and merchant-services operation, and every organisation performing remote key loading into ATMs and POS. (b) Nothing new must be bought because of a 2026 deadline - but the standing v4.x regime (key-block formats, key management, targeted risk analyses, authenticated scanning) keeps demand steady for Thales HSM / PCI-compliant key management and REMOTE KEY INJECTION (which removes the two-custodian site visit and is the standard way estates get and stay compliant), plus terminal management (TMS) for Verifone/Castles fleets and physical ATM security. (c) No new budget trigger. The forward watch item is the next PCI DSS revision arising from the RFC that closed 20/07/2026.
signals.likelihood: Certain for the standing position; a next-version RFC outcome is expected but unscheduled
signals.followup: Deliberately checked and found NO new PCI cliff for 2026 - recording it so the negative is not re-researched. Next run: watch pcisecuritystandards.org for the outcome of the v4.0.1 RFC (closed 20/07/2026) and for any PCI PIN v3.2/v4 announcement, and check Visa/Mastercard CEMEA bulletins, which are the real deadline-setters in this footprint and were NOT accessible in an open search this run.

signals.entity: Balgarska Narodna Banka (BNB) - Bulgarian banks post-euro
signals.signal: [STANDING - dated 2026] Post-euro-changeover position confirmed by the BNB's own euro-area accession Q&A: from 01/01/2026 self-service machines including ATMs dispense ONLY euro banknotes, and the regulatory framework does NOT impose an obligation on banks, after euro introduction, to accept LEV banknotes at self-service machines with a deposit function. That leaves lev deposit handling as a branch/teller process rather than a self-service one.
signals.source_name: Balgarska Narodna Banka - Euro area accession FAQ, 'Evrozonata i platezhnite operatsii' ['The euro area and payment operations']
signals.implies: (a) All Bulgarian banks - UniCredit Bulbank, DSK (OTP), UBB (KBC), Postbank, Fibank, Allianz Bank, plus independent deployers. (b) Because lev deposit is NOT pushed onto self-service, the residual lev exchange volume lands on tellers - which is the classic argument for branch TELLER CASH RECYCLERS to absorb a temporary surge without adding staff, and for kiosk-based exchange where a bank chooses to differentiate. Printec map: Glory / Sesami TCRs (Bank of Cyprus is a footprint reference), NCR recyclers, self-service kiosks, APTRA OptiCash for the post-changeover denomination re-optimisation. (c) The changeover spend has largely happened; the residual 2026 opportunity is teller-side automation and post-changeover cash-cycle re-tuning, not ATM hardware.
signals.likelihood: Certain - position published by the BNB
signals.followup: Belongs to the euro-adoption workstream, not horizon scan - recorded here only because it surfaced during the Bulgarian local-language sweep and confirms no NEW Bulgarian cash-access mandate exists. Cross-check against the euro-adoption checkpoint for this run to avoid double counting.
